title: UPSC Hosts Workshop for Secretaries of State Public Service Commissions on Exam Security, Technology and Recruitment Reforms
subtitle:
More technology needed to check those using technology to beat the system: Dr. Ajay Kumar, Chairman, UPSC
Secretaries bridge policy intent with administrative execution: Shri Shashi Ranjan Kumar, Secretary, UPSC
body_text: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) today hosted a one-day Workshop for Secretaries of State Public Service Commissions at Dholpur House, New Delhi. The workshop brought together the officers who run the day-to-day machinery of recruitment in the States. Secretaries, Joint Secretaries and senior officers of State Commissions from across the country gathered to identify operational bottlenecks, share proven solutions, and work towards harmonising administrative standards nationwide. Organised in pursuance of a decision of the 25th National Conference of Chairpersons of State Public Service Commissions, held in Bengaluru in January 2025, the workshop gives the Secretaries, the operating arm of every Commission, a national platform of their own. It comes at a time when the Commissions face the twin task of conducting large-scale examinations securely and using technology to stay ahead of those who try to misuse it. Addressing the gathering, Dr. Ajay Kumar, Chairman, UPSC, said, "At the UPSC centenary celebrations, the Hon'ble Prime Minister emphasised the importance of sharing best practices among Public Service Commissions, and this workshop is a realisation of that vision. This is a time of reform and innovation, and technology has a big part to play in it. When people use technology to beat the system, the only way is to use more technology to keep a check on them, so that the system remains fair and transparent and the integrity of the examination process is upheld." He also outlined recent initiatives of the Commission, including AI-enabled face authentication of candidates at examination venues, the Universal Registration Number for applicants, digitisation of Departmental Promotion Committee proposals and computerised randomisation of interview boards. Welcoming the participants, Shri Shashi Ranjan Kumar, Secretary, UPSC, said, "This is not a workshop where we teach and you learn. It is a gathering of colleagues who perform the same responsibilities in different circumstances, under the same constitutional obligations. While Chairpersons and Members shape the vision, it is our duty as Secretaries to ensure that operational mechanisms are robust, legally sound, fair and technologically modern. We bridge policy intent with administrative execution." He noted that many State Commissions have developed effective solutions in areas such as digital processing of applications, conduct of examinations in regional languages and grievance redressal, and urged participants to pool these into a shared repository of best practices. He added that, depending on the feedback, the workshop could become an annual feature. Outlining the focus of the working sessions, the UPSC Secretary said, "The presentations rest on four pillars of our shared work: secure examinations that preserve public trust, transparent selection, recruitment rules that keep pace with modern job profiles, and disciplinary advice that balances administrative firmness with natural justice." Following the inaugural session, the workshop moved into four working sessions in which the Commission's branches dealing with examinations, recruitment, recruitment rules, and disciplinary and appeal cases presented their procedures and practices, each followed by an open discussion with the participating officers. The programme concluded with a vote of thanks and a visit to the UPSC Museum. ***** NKR/NM
